chapter: Germany, Paris and return to America
title: Seeing American musicians in Europe
summary: Waters says he kept little contact with the States, but now sees Buddy Tate, Lockjaw, Sweets Edison and others constantly in Europe, earlier mostly Aaron Bridges and Peanuts Holland.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: How often did you see your friends from the States in Europe, and to what extent did you remain in contact through writing with people who didn't come over to Europe? How much did you stay in touch with the old scene?

Well, I didn't stay in touch. Well, that's, like I said before, that's a big fault of mine, my staying in touch with people. I mean that's something I've got to, even at my age now I've still got to learn. But I saw a few American musicians [ ] - not as many as now, which is the last few years, I mean I can see everybody (PS laughs) 'cause everybody's come to Europe. I've seen Buddy Tate so often you'd think he's home when he's (PS laughs) - see Lockjaw all the, I saw Lockjaw in Paris, I saw Lockjaw in Denmark, I saw Lockjaw in Sweden, you know what I mean? And Sweets Edison and all them guys, [I] see all of them nowadays. But then I didn't. It was only a few, see.
Aaron Bridges was there always, pianist, and that's with Bill Coleman. I used to see Peanuts Hucko, I mean Peanuts Holland -
'Cause he was livin' in Sweden, and I worked with Peanuts in Belgium - no, in Holland.
